stem: When categorizing cerebral palsy topographically, what does the term 'diplegic' indicate?

options.text: Only one side of the body is affected
All four limbs are equally affected
The lower limbs are affected significantly more than the upper limbs
The trunk is the only area showing impairment

explanation: Diplegia refers to a distribution where the impairment is predominantly in the legs.
rationale: Focus on the specific distribution of motor impairment between the arms and legs.

optionExplanations.A: This describes hemiplegic cerebral palsy, not diplegic.
optionExplanations.C: Diplegia refers to a distribution where the impairment is predominantly in the legs.
optionExplanations.D: Cerebral palsy classifications typically focus on limb distribution rather than isolated trunk involvement.

source.hint: Focus on the specific distribution of motor impairment between the arms and legs.
